questions.question: What was the authors' solution to CNT motion under the STM tip during high-resolution scans?

options.A: Clamp functionalized MWCNTs beneath few-layer graphite flakes in a CNT–FLG buckypaper composite
options.B: Chemically anchor every tube to Au through Au–S bonds
options.C: Use a high-temperature vacuum bake to remove functional groups
options.D: Embed the tubes in a thick polymer insulating layer

questions.rationale: The few-layer graphite layer mechanically restricts nanotube movement while retaining graphitic support.
questions.evidence_quote: sandwiching them between few layer graphite (FLG) flakes

questions.question: What chemical sequence produced the cross-linked functionalized nanotubes?

options.A: SOCl2 oxidation, nitric acid reduction, then ammonia vapor
options.B: H2SO4/HNO3 oxidation, SOCl2 conversion to –COCl, then diaminopropane treatment
options.C: Hydrogenation, Au-thiol anchoring, and ozone etching
options.D: Diaminopropane first, followed by H2SO4/HNO3 and thermal annealing

questions.rationale: The three-step process oxidized tubes, converted carboxyls to acyl chlorides, then coupled diamine.
questions.evidence_quote: Briefly, in the first step the pristine CNTs were treated in H2SO4/HNO3 (3:1) mixture for 24 h

questions.question: What spectroscopic change indicated increased defect concentration after functionalization?

options.A: A decrease in the infrared –NH peak
options.B: Disappearance of all Raman G-band signal
options.C: An increase in Raman D-peak intensity relative to the G peak (ID/IG)
options.D: A shift of the HOPG work function by 0.25 eV

questions.rationale: The paper uses the increased D/G ratio as a marker of added surface defects.
questions.evidence_quote: an increase in the D peak intensity relative to the G peak (ID/IG)

questions.question: What did the ATR–IR results imply about conversion of –COCl groups to amides?

options.A: Conversion was complete because the –NH feature vanished
options.B: No functional groups were detected in the treated sample
options.C: Only hydroxyl groups remained and no nitrogen-containing signal appeared
options.D: Conversion was incomplete because carboxyl signatures remained alongside an –NH feature

questions.rationale: The spectra showed –NH but retained carboxyl features, indicating incomplete amide conversion.
questions.evidence_quote: the conversion of –COCl groups into amide was not complete

questions.question: How did strongly functionalized regions appear in both topography and conductance maps?

options.A: As surface protrusions accompanied by low-conductance areas
options.B: As depressions with unusually high conductance
options.C: As atomically resolved zigzag bands with symmetric conductance
options.D: As uniform regions indistinguishable from the FLG support

questions.rationale: The paper correlates protrusions with low-conductance map features.
questions.evidence_quote: Functionalized regions show up as protrusions on the nanotube surface and as low

questions.question: Why did the authors interpret low conductance over defective sites as evidence of disruption to the graphitic electronic structure?

options.A: It increases the number of delocalized π electrons by restoring sp2 bonds
options.B: Functionalization converts sp2 carbon to sp3, reducing delocalized π electrons
options.C: It creates a uniform impurity band exactly at the Fermi level
options.D: It eliminates the nanotube's coupling to the substrate

questions.rationale: The sp2-to-sp3 change reduces the delocalized π network and lowers conductance.
questions.evidence_quote: During functionalization the sp2 carbon atoms change to sp3

questions.question: What directional preference did atomic-resolution comparisons reveal for the acid-treatment-related functionalized bands?

options.A: They followed the armchair direction along the tube axis
options.B: They were isotropic with no crystallographic alignment
options.C: They followed the zigzag crystallographic direction around the nanotube circumference
options.D: They aligned with the nanotube axis regardless of lattice direction

questions.rationale: The measured functionalized bands followed the zigzag direction.
questions.evidence_quote: these follow the zigzag direction along the nanotube circumference.

questions.question: What did the authors infer from the asymmetric dI/dV region with higher conductance at positive bias?

options.A: It proved the region was defect-free and metallic
options.B: It was definitively caused by the FLG substrate band gap
options.C: It indicated a local n-doping shift of exactly 0.25 eV
options.D: Its origin was unclear, but impurity states at functionalized or defect sites were a possible cause

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly say the asymmetry's origin is unclear and mention impurity states as a possibility.
questions.evidence_quote: The origin of this asymmetry is not clear

questions.question: What approximate global Fermi-level shift did the LDOS-minimum map indicate in mostly functional-group-free regions?

options.D: No measurable shift from the Fermi level

questions.rationale: The LDOS minimum map indicated strong p-doping with approximately this shift.
questions.evidence_quote: with a Fermi level shift of around 0.25 eV.

questions.question: What caveat did the authors attach to interpreting the LDOS-minimum map in low-conductance areas?

options.A: The energy resolution is too low to distinguish positive from negative bias
options.B: The damaged sp2 lattice makes the surface electronic structure unknown, so interpretation is not straightforward
options.C: The regions were obscured by the graphite support
options.D: The map cannot reveal the local dI/dV minimum

questions.rationale: They caution that severe lattice damage makes the surface electronic structure unknown.
questions.evidence_quote: the interpretation of this map is not straightforward in the low conductance regions
